thread:
maria: Heads up — noticed the Endpoint Dashboard’s per-slice view shows p99 for /v1/generate at 220ms but the global service p95 is 340ms. Feels backwards.
aj: Huh. Is that the slice where we route to the variant pool? Could be sampling/rollup mismatch.
kevin: Can you paste the slice filter you used? Sometimes the dashboard UI hides the retry traces.
maria: Filter: `route:/v1/generate && variant:smallbatch && region:us-west` — here's the query from the console: ```select quantile(0.99, latency_ms) from endpoint_metrics where route='/v1/generate' and variant='smallbatch' and region='us-west'``` 
lina: If per-slice is only sampling successful final responses and the global view includes retries+fallbacks, p95 could be higher globally. We had a similar discrepancy with favoured routing last month.
aj: Also check that the per-slice rollup used `tdigest` compressed hist vs global which uses raw buckets. Compression biases can invert tails.
kevin: Good call. I ran the raw count: slice has 12k samples, global has 120k. Sampling weight is consistent, but I see `route_weight` label missing on the per-slice series — that breaks the merge key during rollup.
maria: So when rollup merges, series without `route_weight` get coalesced into a broader aggregate and that can inflate the tail? I thought missing labels usually just get dropped.
kevin: Our merge logic falls back to default bucketization when labels differ. If label sets mismatch we currently expand the histogram domain which mixes cold-start latencies from other pools.
lina: That's the bug then. UX shows the per-slice table but the backend used a different keyset for the percentiles calculation. We should either show a banner about label mismatch or normalize labels before computing percentiles.
aj: Quick diagnostic: add this query to confirm label cardinality: ```count_distinct(tags) from endpoint_metrics where route='/v1/generate' group by variant,region``` — if label sets differ across granularity we can reproduce.
maria: I ran that — `variant:smallbatch` in us-west had 2 tagsets: one with `route_weight` and one without. Looks like an intermediary router strips the label for a subset of requests during bursts.
kevin: Suggestion: in the pipeline, when we do rollups, treat missing numeric labels as `__missing__` instead of dropping. That keeps keys stable and avoids domain expansion.
lina: UX action: add small orange warning on the slice card: "percentile rollup used heterogeneous label sets — results may be inconsistent". Also add a link to docs explaining label hygiene.
aj: Ops action: open an infra ticket to find which router strips `route_weight` under high concurrency. Likely the fast-path proxy.
maria: I'll file the infra ticket and add the warning PR for the console. Who wants to own the stats normalization change in the rollup pipeline?
kevin: I'll take the pipeline patch. Plan: 1) quick hotfix to normalize missing labels as `__missing__` 2) add a unit test that simulates mixed tagsets and ensures percentiles don't invert 3) dashboard warning.
sre-bot: Incident created — #INC-2026: proxy-fastpath-drops-route_weight (priority: P2) assigned to infra-team. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026 :rotating_light:
maria: Thanks — assigning console PR to @lina. We should also surface in release notes for the next console deploy.
aj: Cool. TL;DR: discrepancy caused by label mismatch during rollup -> pipeline normalization + console warning + infra ticket. Good catch.
kevin: I'll push the normalization branch today and ping for review. If anyone can add a small synthetic test case in the dashboard e2e that would help catch regressions.
lina: Will do the warning copy and a short docs blurb. Maria — can you paste the example trace sample that lost the label? Want to include in the infra ticket.
maria: Pasting 2 sample traces (ids): `trace:Zxq-9` (has route_weight), `trace:Zxq-13` (missing route_weight). Both from 2025-08-02 14:22 UTC. Included in the ticket.
kevin: Excellent. I'll follow up with a short note in #eng-platform when the normalization is in staging.
maria: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
